title: Generation of full-length circRNA libraries for Oxford Nanopore long-read sequencing
author: Steffen Fuchs
materials: Continue the program of the thermocycler ( 65 °C for 00:10:00 ) then place the sample On ice

Negative poly(A) selection Oligo(dT) coupled beads will be used to negatively select the remaining polyadenylated linear RNAs. This step follows the manufacturer’s protocol of the NEBNext ® Poly(A) mRNA Magnetic Isolation Module (NEB #7490) with modifications. This further enriches for circRNAs.

The enriched circRNA fraction will be used to create a cDNA library using the SMARTer cDNA synthesis kit (Takara #634926) following the manufacturer’s instructions with modifications. To transcribe circRNAs without poly(A) sequences the 3’SMART CDS Primer IIA, which has a 3’oligo(dT) has to be replaced by a primer with random nucleotides at the 3’ end. The cDNA library is amplified with LongAmp Taq 2x master mix (NEB # M0287S) using the SMARTer PCR primer from the cDNA synthesis kit.

cDNA generation Set up the following PCR program in a thermocycler: 3 min. at 72°C 10 min. at 25°C Hold at 42°C (this is when the reverse transcription mix gets added) 90 min. at 42°C 10 min. at 70°C Hold at 4°C
Use 1 µL of enriched RNA from step 9.10 as input for reverse transcription using the Maxima H Minus RT kit (Thermo #K1682) without DNase treatment.

steps.title: Thaw RNA and reagents
steps.instruction: Thaw 7 µg total RNA on ice, thaw one aliquot of rRNA‑depletion oligos on ice, bring Agencourt RNA Clean XP beads to room temperature for at least 30 min, and set a heat block to 65 °C for later RNaseH incubation.

steps.title: Prepare RNaseH and hybridization mixes
steps.instruction: Prepare the RNaseH mix (without enzyme) and the hybridization mix keeping an RNA:oligo ratio of 1:4‑5; program the thermocycler: 95 °C hold, 95 °C 3 min, ramp 0.1 °C/s to 65 °C, 65 °C 5 min, hold at 65 °C, then 65 °C 10 min.

steps.title: Hybridize RNA with depletion oligos
steps.instruction: Add the hybridization mix to the RNA sample and incubate in the programmed thermocycler until the 65 °C hold is reached.

steps.title: Add RNaseH enzyme
steps.instruction: Add RNaseH enzyme to the RNaseH mix, vortex, spin down, then add 20 µL of this RNaseH‑containing mix to the hybridized sample, mix, spin down, and return the tube to the thermocycler.

steps.title: First bead clean‑up
steps.instruction: Vortex RNA Clean XP beads until homogeneously brown, add 60 µL (1×) beads to the RNaseH‑treated sample, mix, incubate 5 min at room temperature, place on magnet 5 min, discard supernatant, wash twice with 200 µL 80 % ethanol (30 s each), air‑dry 5 min (avoid over‑drying), elute with 38.5 µL H₂O, incubate 5 min, magnet 5 min, transfer 37.5 µL supernatant to a new tube.

steps.title: DNase digestion of depletion oligos
steps.instruction: Prepare DNase mix, add 17.5 µL to the cleaned‑up sample, mix, incubate 30 min at 37 °C in a thermocycler, then place on ice.

steps.title: Second bead clean‑up and elution
steps.instruction: Perform a second bead clean‑up as above using 55 µL RNA Clean XP beads, elute in 15.5 µL H₂O, and keep 14.5 µL on ice for downstream circRNA enrichment.

steps.title: Polyadenylate linear RNAs
steps.instruction: Prepare poly‑A polymerase mix (volumes not specified), add to the 14.5 µL saved RNA, mix, spin down, incubate 30 min at 37 °C in a thermocycler, then clean‑up with 20 µL RNA Clean XP beads (1:1 ratio) and elute in 18 µL H₂O, keeping 17 µL for RNaseR treatment on ice.

steps.title: RNaseR treatment of poly‑A RNA
steps.instruction: Prepare RNaseR mix: 17 µL poly‑adenylated RNA, 2 µL 10× reaction buffer, 0.5 µL RNaseR (20 U/µL), 0.5 µL RNase inhibitor (40 U/µL) to 20 µL total; incubate 30 min at 37 °C, then clean‑up with 20 µL RNA Clean XP beads (1:1) and elute in 21 µL, saving 20 µL for negative poly‑A selection on ice.

steps.title: Capture poly‑A RNA with oligo(dT) beads
steps.instruction: Bring NEBNext Poly(A) mRNA Magnetic Isolation Module to room temperature, vortex oligo(dT) beads, wash 20 µL beads twice with 100 µL RNA bead binding buffer on a magnetic rack, resuspend in 20 µL binding buffer, add to the RNaseR‑treated RNA, incubate 5 min at 65 °C, hold 4 °C, mix, incubate 5 min at room temperature, place on magnet 5 min, transfer the supernatant (non‑poly‑A, enriched circRNA) to a new tube on ice.

steps.title: Bead clean‑up of enriched circRNA
steps.instruction: Clean the enriched circRNA fraction with 40 µL RNA Clean XP beads (1:1), elute in 6 µL H₂O, and keep 5 µL for cDNA library creation and QC on ice.

steps.title: Hybridization for reverse transcription
steps.instruction: Prepare the hybridization mix (volumes not specified), incubate in the thermocycler until the 42 °C hold is reached, then add the reverse‑transcription mix (see step 19) and continue the program to the 4 °C hold; keep the sample on ice.

steps.title: PCR amplify cDNA
steps.instruction: Prepare PCR mix: 6.8 µL SMARTer PCR primer (12 µM, 0.8 µM final), 4 µL cDNA, 50 µL LongAmp Taq 2× Master Mix (1× final), 39.2 µL H₂O to 100 µL total; run: 95 °C 30 s, 25 cycles of 95 °C 15 s, 62 °C 15 s, 65 °C 2 min, final extension 65 °C 2 min, hold 4 °C.

steps.title: AMPure bead size selection
steps.instruction: Add 80 µL AMPure XP beads (0.8:1 ratio) to the PCR product, mix, incubate, place on magnet, discard supernatant, wash, elute in 31 µL H₂O, keep 30 µL for Oxford Nanopore library preparation and QC; store remaining cDNA at –20 °C.

steps.title: Quantify library concentration
steps.instruction: Measure library concentration with a Qubit fluorometer using the BR dsDNA assay (1 µL of amplified cDNA library).

steps.title: Determine library size
steps.instruction: Run 2 µL of diluted amplified cDNA library on a Fragment Analyzer (hs NGS Fragment kit) to obtain average fragment length.

steps.title: Calculate library molarity
steps.instruction: Use the Quantification result and average length in the Promega Biomath Calculator (DNA µg → pmol) to obtain fmol; aim for 1 µg (100‑200 fmol) input for Oxford Nanopore SQK‑LSK109, optionally up to 1000 fmol for low‑abundance circRNAs.

steps.title: Validate circRNA enrichment by qRT‑PCR
steps.instruction: Prepare reverse‑transcription mix (1 µL enriched RNA, 12.5 µL H₂O, 0.5 µL random hexamer 100 µM, 1 µL 10 mM dNTPs, 4 µL 5× RT buffer, 1 µL Maxima H‑Minus enzyme) to 20 µL; incubate 25 °C 10 min, 50 °C 15 min, 85 °C 5 min, hold 4 °C; dilute 1 µL cDNA 1:10, prepare qPCR master mix (5 µL 2× FastStart Essential DNA Green Master, 0.5 µL 10 µM forward primer, 0.5 µL 10 µM reverse primer, 3 µL H₂O, 1 µL cDNA) to 10 µL; run 50 °C 2 min, 95 °C 10 min, then 40 cycles of 95 °C 15 s, 60 °C 1 min, followed by melt‑curve analysis; compare Ct values of enriched sample versus mock control.

steps.title: End‑preparation for Nanopore library
steps.instruction: Prepare DNA ends according to the Oxford Nanopore protocol (using up to 1000 fmol of input RNA‑derived cDNA).

steps.title: Native barcode ligation and pooling
steps.instruction: Ligate native barcodes (EXP‑NBD104/114) using 22.5 µL of the end‑prepped reaction, clean‑up with magnetic beads, elute in 11 µL (10 µL for pooling, 1 µL for concentration measurement), measure concentration with Qubit, calculate molarity, and pool equimolar amounts (typically 400 fmol per sample, 4‑5 samples).

steps.title: Adapter ligation and bead clean‑up
steps.instruction: Ligate Nanopore adapters, then clean‑up with 0.8× volume of AMPure XP beads; perform three washes with the short‑fragment buffer, elute, and measure final library concentration (target 15‑25 ng/µL, 30‑70 fmol/µL).

steps.title: Prime and load flow cell
steps.instruction: Prime the MinION (MK1C) flow cell, wait 5 min, then load 5‑50 fmol of library (up to 200 fmol in practice); keep the flow cell at 4 °C until sequencing starts.

steps.title: Optional flow‑cell wash and reload
steps.instruction: After ~1 day, perform a nuclease flush with the Flow Cell Wash Kit (EXP‑WSH004), re‑prime the flow cell, and reload 200‑300 fmol of library to recover pores and increase total reads.

steps.title: Base‑call raw Nanopore data
steps.instruction: Run Guppy (v22.05.8) with standard parameters to convert .fast5 files to passed .fastq files.

steps.title: Trim adapters with cutadapt
steps.instruction: Execute two cutadapt commands: (1) cutadapt -e 0.2 -m 1 -g AAGCAGTGGTATCAACGCAGAGTAC -o FileName_5pTrimmed.fastq.gz FileName.fastq.gz; (2) cutadapt -e 0.2 -m 1 -a GTACTCTGCGTTGATACCACTGCTT -o TrimmedFileName.fastq.gz FileName_5pTrimmed.fastq.gz.

steps.title: Identify circRNAs with CIRI‑long
steps.instruction: Run CIRI‑long call: CIRI‑long call -i FileName.fastq.gz -o step1 -r genome.fa -p SampleName -a genome.gtf -t 10; then collapse: CIRI‑long collapse -i SampleFile.lst -o step2 -p SampleName -r genome.fa -a genome.gtf -t 10.

steps.title: Align reads and generate BAM
steps.instruction: Align with minimap2: minimap2 -ax splice -t 20 -uf -k14 genome_index FileName.fastq.gz > FileName.sam; convert and sort: samtools view -b FileName.sam | samtools sort > FileName.bam; index: samtools index FileName.bam.

description: Limitations and challenges A limitation of the protocol is the relatively high input of RNA of 7 µg. While this amount of RNA worked best in our experiments, we also tried successfully only 3-5 µg. Further, in general the Nanopore sequencing platform produces less reads than Illumina-based short read techniques, especially when using the MinION. That means lowly abundant circRNAs might not be detected by our sequencing protocol. Limitations of CIRI-Long are that the alignment parameters cannot be modified and bam files containing the aligned reads are not conserved. Further, there is no option to detect fusion circRNAs derived from fusion genes (distant genes, genes located on different chromosomes). Troubleshooting Below we provide assistance and recommendations for problems that can occur during this protocol and the analysis of the data. circRNA enrichment Step 7 RNaseR treatment: if the enrichment of circRNAs seems to be insufficient, a longer incubation with RNaseR could be tried. Step 11 PCR amplification: if the obtained amount of cDNA is much lower than expected, the volume of the PCR reaction and/or the amount of PCR cycles could be increased. Step 12 Fragment size selection: if the size of the circRNAs of interest that should be enriched is much higher or lower, the ratio of beads to DNA could be adapted. A higher ratio will lead to retention of smaller fragments, a lower ratio will select for longer fragments. Validation of circRNA enrichment While we provide a selection of primers covering different RNA species that should be depleted by the workflow, further transcripts can be checked by qRT-PCR in this step. Nanopore sequencing Care has to be taken to not introduce air bubbles while priming or loading a flow cell, since this will damage pores irreversibly. The pore activity should be closely monitored while sequencing. If a lot of inactive pores accumulate, a flow cell wash could be performed as described above.
